excitation_report: Noise sigma=0.1 on dN_dt (yardstick). Full child-vs-parent system comparison on the N trajectory over t in [0,120], 200 integration samples. The new mechanism (child minus parent = P_i*(c*N^2/(1+b*N) - beta*N), i.e. the disease-modulated mortality and infected excess-mortality coupling to the P_i state) shifts the target trajectory by up to 0.609, i.e. 6.09*sigma, well above the k=5 threshold; strongest near t~105 where prevalence has built up and N settles. Dominant terms (logistic growth ~25, Holling-III predation up to a=5, mate-limitation up to m=2, saturating disease mortality) are all far above sigma. Passes.

rationale: Typed ode_system contract inherited verbatim: states [N, P_i], their two RHS, ICs {N:10, P_i:0.01}, target N. Parameters chosen for a biologically sensible self-limiting herbivore trajectory from N0=10 toward a stable abundance below K=100: r=0.8 (growth timescale ~1/r), theta=1.5 mild super-logistic crowding, Holling-III predation a=5 with half-saturation N_h=30, Allee mate-limitation m=2 with N_a=5 (per-capita loss m/(N+N_a) high at low density), saturating disease term c=0.002,b=0.01 keeping c*N^2/(1+b*N) modest vs growth, and disease dynamics sigma=1.0/gamma=0.02 tuned so prevalence P_i builds to an endemic level (~0.6-0.8) so the new coupling term is excited; beta=0.1 infected excess mortality. Window t in [0,120] (400 pts) captures the full approach to steady state and the peak divergence from the parent. excitation_check (is_ode) confirms the new term reaches 6.09*sigma.

scenario_text: A grazing herbivore population inhabits a pasture with finite carrying capacity determined by fixed vegetation availability. Growth is rapid when the population is small but slows as crowding intensifies and resources per individual dwindle. Field counts are recorded from an initial size well below capacity. The objective is to capture the self-limiting approach to a stable abundance.
